# NOW — the Chronicle

**BOOK I — THE HOUSE OF MENDERS · Chapter 3 — The Undercroft · dusk, the day after the letters came**

- **Where:** Saint Ysolde's, the House of Menders; on the first step of the undercroft stair, behind the iron-banded door at the dark end of the infirmary hall, at dusk.
- **The quest:** *The List.* The Confessors have come for the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's with a list: Darrow first, Hollis second. The named are to be taken down the Steps to the Oathspire and made to kneel where everyone can watch, which would say the Ninth drowned for its own bad faith, and would tear the thread in Darrow's knee. What stands between them and the hall is Old Mercy, the sanctuary bell: while it rings at dawn and dusk, no blade passes the gate and no name under it is taken down against its will. Miss one ringing and the law lapses till the next, and Sister Pell, who rings it, is very old. At the gate, Confessor Ivo Marrant read his names at the bars, and two of his men came through the wicket before the bell rang, late. Now five grey cloaks are camped on the lower terrace below the gate, and the sixth holds the winch-house, the cage and Rae's cart, so the road is theirs. Marrant's price: the Captain of the Ninth comes down and kneels, and the rest of the paper goes back in his cloak. Darrow went to the bars and gave him his name and his face. Marrant says he will wait.
- **What Darrow is fighting right now:** The soft season, and the waiting. The knee is held and still soft. Benedek lies Hollowed in the Grey Cot, and nobody passed in the night; the Confessor's word for it, ember witchcraft, is in the hall now, and the hall wants a hand to fit it. Under it is the thing he has said only to Maelis: a lad who cannot answer has no will for the bell to keep.
- **Just happened (Between):** *Room Under It.* He did not have to turn round to know she had been watching the knee the whole time, and not them. "Still one," she said.
- **Earlier today, in order:** *Nine Down* (Scene): "One," said Maelis. He put his foot down into it.
- **With him:** Maelis Vorne (Behind the Captain on the undercroft stair at dusk, without a lamp; her count still at one.) · Ser Hollis Garrow (At the Grey Cot with the lad's hand in his; he watched the undercroft door open and said nothing.) · Wren Ashdown (A step below the Captain on the undercroft stair with the lamp held out over the second step. She has asked him to come back up, and keeps a new count: times the Captain has said a decent thing on a stair, one.)
- **Also here:** Ser Aldric Vane (Wrote again from Calden, before the list was read: Calden says the Ninth broke faith when its captain turned out of the line for one of his…) · Ser Benedek Orrin (Lay in the Grey Cot, his hand in Hollis's.) · Confessor Ivo Marrant (Came to the bars at the dawn bell to ask for the Captain's answer, read it at the gate, thanked him for his candour, and sent it down the S…) · Mother Ione (Heard the Captain's answer in the chapel and asked whether it was true or only right; set it for dusk; at dusk had the House sup at the kit…) · Sister Pell (Rang the hours through the night and came down between every bell to sit by the undercroft door; heard nothing come or go; told Hollis she…)
- **The tales:** Tale 1 — Quickstep (1 of 3 told)
- **Against him:** About twenty riders under a banner that is not grey are on the Holloway; something below the hall draws on it every night.
- **Next:** Down the undercroft stair at the Mender's count, and back up it.
- **Open choice:** none.
